new_statements.quote: ACENTO. El acento tónico carga generalmente en la sílaba radical de la palabra; si esta es compuesta conserva el acento en la palabra principal del compuesto, como: uóp, azotar; pauóp, arrear; tukpauóp, hacer arrear; en las cuales el acento tónico está en la palabra uóp.
new_statements.translation: ACCENT. Tonic stress generally falls on the root syllable of the word; if the word is a compound, it keeps the stress on the principal word of the compound, e.g. uóp 'to whip'; pauóp 'to drive (animals)'; tukpauóp 'to make (someone) drive'; in all of which the tonic stress is on the word uóp.
new_statements.citation: Belmar, Francisco. 1902. Lenguas indígenas del Estado de Oaxaca: Estudio del idioma ayook. Oaxaca: Imprenta del Comercio.
new_statements.locator: Estudio (grammar part), section 'ACENTO.', p. 7 (archive.org scan estudiodelidioma01belm, PDF p. 49; verified on the rendered page image Belmar1902_pages/)
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Opened via the page image Belmar1902_pages/printed page "-7-" of the Estudio) and the two text layers ( lines 3367-3371; extracted text). The page image reads exactly: "ACENTO. / El acento tónico carga generalmente en la sílaba radical de la palabra; si esta es compuesta conserva el acento en la palabra principal del compuesto, como: uóp, azotar; pauóp, arrear; tukpauóp, hacer arrear; en las cuales el acento tónico está en la palabra uóp." The scanned layers garble the examples (uój), flauóp, hikfiauóp) but the image confirms uóp / pauóp / tukpauóp as quoted. Surrounding section (pp. 6-7): "DIVISION DE LAS PALABRAS" says primitive words are generally monosyllabic (atz, yoz) and polysyllable…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Stress falls on the root syllable (Mixe roots are mostly monosyllabic; affixes such as pa-, tuk- are unstressed); in compounds and derived words the stress stays on the head root, e.g. tuk-pa-uóp.
new_statements.domain_note: Word level (simple and compound/derived words); no remarks on phrase stress or citation forms. Belmar's data mix Quintana's colonial Juquila ('mohtuau') Mixe with Villa Alta (Totontepec-area) material, so the statement is a 1902 pan-'ayook' generalisation rather than a modern description of Juquila proper.
new_statements.identity_note: Belmar 1902 is filed by Glottolog under juqu1238 ('Midland Mixe in Juquila'), but Belmar explicitly draws on Quintana's colonial Juquila Mixe ('dialecto mohtuau.. de Juquila') and on the Villa Alta (Totontepec-area, toto1263) variety, so his accent rule is a pan-'ayook' statement. Glottolog 5 places Chuxnabán Mixe (chux1234; Jany's and Dagostino's 'Chuxnabán Mixe', ISO pxm, mun. Quetzaltepec) as a dialect of juqu1238, so Jany 2011 (held) and Dagostino 2025 are first-hand for this languoid but give no placement rule. The SIL mxq-tagged Miller 1947 manuscripts are based on San Lucas Camotlán data. Santos Martínez 2013 ('mixe de Metepec') describes an agencia of Totontepec (toto1263), not this language.

new_statements.quote: ACENTO. El acento tónico carga generalmente en la sílaba radical de la palabra; si esta es compuesta conserva el acento en la palabra principal del compuesto, como: uóp, azotar; pauóp, arrear; tukpauóp, hacer arrear; en las cuales el acento tónico está en la palabra uóp.
new_statements.translation: ACCENT. The tonic accent generally falls on the root syllable of the word; if the word is compound it keeps the accent on the principal word of the compound, e.g. uóp 'to whip'; pauóp 'to drive (animals)'; tukpauóp 'to make (someone) drive'; in all of which the tonic accent is on the word uóp.
new_statements.citation: Belmar, Francisco (1902). Estudio del Idioma Ayook. Oaxaca: Imprenta del Comercio. 286 pp.
new_statements.locator: Estudio (grammar part), section 'ACENTO.', printed p. 7 (= PDF p. 49 of the archive.org scan estudiodelidioma01belm); text verified against the page image
new_statements.relation_note: This is the very work the existing_statement was taken from; re-reading the page image confirms the quotation verbatim (the scanned layers garble the examples as 'uój)', 'flauóp', 'hikfiauóp', but the image reads uóp, pauóp, tukpauóp). Same placement (root syllable, morphologically determined) as the existing statement; the catalog record itself has an empty rule field, so this fills it rather than contradicting it.
new_statements.rule_in_words: Word stress falls on the root syllable; prefixes (pa-, tuk-) do not attract it, and in compounds/derivatives the stress stays on the principal (root) element (uóp > pa-uóp > tuk-pa-uóp all stressed on uóp). Belmar hedges with 'generalmente'. The preceding 'DIVISION DE LAS PALABRAS' (pp. 6-7) says primitive words are usually monosyllabic (atz, yoz) and polysyllables are divided by their morphological formation (yak-tziu, tuk-yak-tziu), which is why the placement is root-based rather than positional.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Not mentioned. The earlier 'DUPLICACIÓN DE VOCALES' and 'DIPTONGOS' paragraphs (Estudio pp. 3-4, djvu lines 3031-3056: 'aa, se pronuncia cargando el acento en la primera á, y repitiendo suavemente la segunda'; 'ia, se pronuncia cargando el acento en la a') describe prominence inside rearticulated-vowel and diphthong nuclei within a single syllable, not word-level secondary stress.
new_statements.exceptions: Only the hedge 'generalmente' (generally); no explicit exceptions listed.
new_statements.identity_note: Belmar 1902 is a pan-'ayook' (Mixe) grammar. Its own preface (pp. XVII-XVIII) quotes Quintana's three-way division (Mohtuau, Cotún, Huhmah) and the phonology repeatedly contrasts Quintana's 'dialecto móhtuau' (colonial Juquila Mixe, the basis for Glottolog's filing under juqu1238/mxq) with the speech of the 'núcleo de los pueblos del Distrito de Villa-Alta' and Totontepec (pp. 2-5 of the Estudio). The ACENTO paragraph itself is not attributed to any particular town or dialect, so the root-stress rule should be taken as Belmar's general Mixe statement with mixed Juquila/Villa Alta data behind it, hence medium rather than high confidence for Juquila Mixe specifically.

sources.note: NOT this language: San Miguel Metepec is an agencia of Totontepec Villa de Morelos, 'Mixe alto del norte' (pp. 6-9) = Totontepec Mixe (toto1263). Its rule (sec. 4.4, p. 233): stress on the final syllable when it has a long, long-glottalised or rearticulated vowel, otherwise on the penult (moraic trochee built from the right edge).
